questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted a more international education experience, and I wanted to develop both academically and personally. Therefore it was important for me, that it was a bit further away from home, so I could challenge myself. I also wanted to study at a place where English was the primary language, so I could practice that while I was gone. Furthermore I chose UNSW, as they sounded like they had a good public health program.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The school communicated very clearly, so it was easy to find information of importance for my exchange

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Emails and 0-week / introduction week (with mandatory attendance to an introduction seminar for all new exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of people wanting accommodation, so it can be pretty competitive. And can also be a bit of a stressfactor that the host university doesn't really help with accommodations. When the is said, I did find my accommodation through a teams meeting, where they come with recommendations for different sites and so on, you could look at.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be hard to find before arriving in Sydney, many do not find it beforehand - but uses flatmates and other sites. I was lucky to find a accommodation that UNSW recommended, so I knew they weren't a fraud.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Hard to find - very much on your own, as UNSW don't offer exchange students housing

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was mostly about settoing up of my microsoft account and getting my student id number. Mostly was done through KU and mobility online beforehand.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mail, number and teams meetings - where they gave information

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got nearly everything approved by both home and host university. I only had one course rejected by KU - which I still have a hard time understanding why

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not much - it was pretty straightforward

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was good, but it wasn't as challenging as at home. But in some way that is nice, as there are also a lot of other things going on, and you need to get used to a new place to live and more.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is easier than at home, but their way of both teaching and their exams are different that I am used to. We had a lot of assignments as part of our grade, where we often had to pick our own topics. So the assignments/exams didn't quite fit all the lectures. Often you didn't really get to use the things the went through in class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: See above + they had better possibility to follow along online - the institution had a way better setup for it than we have.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Sydney Environment 
Health Organisations, Strategy and Change
Comparative Healthcare Systems
Infectious Diseases Challenges: Epidemiology and Control

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
In general for all students I would say that Introduction to Sydney Environment is cool, as you get into a wide range of knowledge on Sydney. 

In a public health point of view the three other courses might be more relevant.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The cost of the visa did change from 2024-2025, so I was surprised that just this by itself was around 7.300 kr.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Greens depending on season are more expensive, Gas I far less expensive. But in general a lot of things is within the same price range as in DK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were over 300 different clubs you could register yourself in. I myself played along with one of the football teams while I was there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you like sports ARC has different programs, where you can try out a lot of different sports

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try to travel, I went to Melbourne and did the Great Ocean Road (can very much recommend). I also took a trip to Uluru (also a big reccomondation) - otherwise rent a car from time to time, there are a lot of great places within reach of some hours by car (Blue mountain, Hunter Valley, Jervis bay and more)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine, I was a bit surprised that the university was very multicultural  - which is also seen in the very many different non-academic clubs.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't really get to meet that many local students - mostly in my sports

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were many students that needed to translate the lectures directly by an Ipad which could be a bit disturbing (also weird, as they need an English test to study there) .

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Aussies openness, the sporty and outdoorsy culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remember to save some money up yourself, so you are not relying on grants for the trip to be possible (that feels a bit safer and more relaxing), be open minded and remember to do a lot of things you might not normally do. Also you can maybe relax a bit more regarding the subjects, as the subject are a bit easier than home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go for at social club or participate in one of the many free running clubs around the city (Coogee Run Club, Unofficial run club or Sydney Run Club.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to live in another country, getting to know a lot of different people and gain a more international perspective on things. Also to practice and use my English a lot more than home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not sure, it has ben delightful! There has only been minor things, that have been challenging and nothing really necessary to mention.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
